steps.observation: You have 900 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Here’s a plan for a 15-minute (900 s) deep-dive into how a Transformer works, plus the core concepts you’d cover in each segment:

0–2 min: Why Transformers?  
• Past approaches (RNNs, CNNs) struggle with long-range dependencies or parallelism.  
• Transformers solve both by using attention rather than recurrence or convolutions.

2–5 min: From tokens to vectors  
• Tokenization: split text into tokens (words, subwords, bytes).  
• Embedding layer: map each token to a high-dimensional vector.  
• Positional encoding: add a fixed or learned vector so the model “knows” token order.

5–9 min: Self-Attention mechanism  
• Query, Key, Value: for each token vector x we compute  
    Q = x·W_Q, K = x·W_K, V = x·W_V  
• Scaled dot-product: score(i,j) = (Q_i·K_j) / sqrt(d_k)  
• Softmax over j gives attention weights; output_i = Σ_j softmax(score(i,j))·V_j  
• Intuition: each output combines all inputs, weighted by relevance.

9–12 min: Multi-Head, Feed-Forward, and Layer Structure  
• Multi-head attention: run several self-attentions in parallel with different W_Q,K,V; concatenate results.  
• Position-wise feed-forward: two-layer MLP applied independently to each position.  
• Residual connections + layer normalization after attention and after feed-forward to ease training.  
• Stack N identical layers for rich, hierarchical representations.

12–14 min: Encoder vs. Decoder  
• Encoder: N layers of self-attention + feed-forward; produces contextualized representations for all input tokens.  
• Decoder: similar layers but with two attention blocks per layer—  
    1) masked self-attention (prevents “peeking” at future tokens),  
    2) encoder–decoder attention (lets decoder attend to encoder outputs).  
• Final linear+softmax to predict next token in auto-regressive generation.

14–15 min: Wrap-up & Intuition  
• Key insight: attention lets every token “talk to” every other in one shot, fully parallelizable.  
• Multi-head captures different types of relationships.  
• Residual & normalization ensure stable, deep models.  
• Result: state-of-the-art in translation, summarization, language modeling, and beyond.

Conceptual takeaways:  
1. Transform input into embeddings + positional info.  
2. Use self-attention to compute context-aware representations.  
3. Stack multi-headed attention + feed-forwards with residuals for depth.  
4. In decoding, mask future tokens and attend to encoder outputs for generation.  

That’s the high-level workflow of a Transformer neural network!
